measures.action: Use the fire extinguisher on the burning object before the fire grows.

effect.text: Engineering proposal (hypothesis): the engine puts out the fire where it started at that moment. The extinguisher stands in the scene; its type, agent and effectiveness on this fire are not documented here.
effect.src: Hypothesis; no test in the sources used

measures.action: Smother the burning object with a fire blanket (cut its oxygen).

effect.text: Engineering proposal (hypothesis): the engine puts out the fire where it started at that moment. Smothering works because a flame needs an oxidiser (stated by the experiments of the archive, not tested for this fire).
effect.src: Hypothesis; flame needs fuel and oxidiser (stated, not measured, for this place)

measures.action: Put a fire-blocking barrier between the pad and safety cone 1 so a fire cannot cross.

effect.text: Engineering proposal (hypothesis): the engine removes this connection. A barrier breaks the continuous fuel path that the model assumes. No test of such a barrier exists in the sources used.
effect.src: Hypothesis; flame spread needs continuous fuel (stated, not measured, for this place)

gaps: The fire site is a procedural scene (pad, extinguisher, four cones, bare ground), not a model of a real place: distances and objects are illustrative.

Worst case: the liquid fuel is assumed to spill across the 1.3 m of bare ground and carry the flame to each cone. Real spill spread, radiant ignition and wind are not modelled and no dataset in the archive covers them.
No PSI/NTRS combustion test of a fuel pan or a safety cone exists; the PSI experiments are microgravity tests, so 1 g on Earth is the least evidenced side of the lab.
The extinguisher is steel (treated as non-combustible); its agent and effectiveness are not documented, so putting a fire out is a hypothesis.
Energetic components: none in this scene (no tank or battery), so there is no rupture.
Detection and the response of people are not modelled: the times are for an unattended fire.
